editorial:
Imagine living in a wealthy California town where everything looks perfect on the outside, but the kids are totally lost on the inside. You will follow a group of high schoolers who have plenty of money but almost no attention from their parents. The vibe is very dreamy and slow, making you feel exactly how these teens feel: bored, confused, and just looking for something to happen. You get to see how they drift through their days, getting into trouble and making bad choices just to feel some kind of spark in their lives.

The acting feels very natural, almost like you are watching a home movie of real people. While the story does not have a big, shocking twist or fast action, it captures that awkward feeling of growing up perfectly. Some might find it too slow, but if you like character studies, you will love it. For the best experience, you should try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to soak in the sunny scenery. If you prefer owning your movies, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great move for the high visual quality.
endingExplained: The movie ends without a big happy resolution because life for these teens is still messy. You see the main characters still struggling with their identities and bad habits. There is no sudden fix for their broken homes or their loneliness. Instead, it wraps up by showing that they are stuck in a cycle of boredom and rebellion, leaving you to realize that they might stay this way for a long time.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves coming-of-age stories and moody atmospheres.
